school: Quantum Field Theory, Particle Physics, Statistical Mechanics
legacy: Chen Ning Yang is one of the most influential theoretical physicists of the twentieth century. His work fundamentally transformed modern physics, particularly through the development of Yang-Mills theory, which became the mathematical foundation of the Standard Model of particle physics. His discoveries helped reshape humanity's understanding of the fundamental forces governing nature and influenced generations of physicists worldwide.
earlyLife: Yang was born in Hefei, Anhui, China. The son of mathematician Yang Wu-chih, he developed a strong interest in mathematics and science from a young age. He studied at the National Southwestern Associated University during the difficult years of the Second World War and later earned a master's degree from National Tsing Hua University. In 1946 he moved to the United States to pursue doctoral studies at the University of Chicago under Edward Teller, where he was also influenced by Enrico Fermi.
scientificField: Theoretical Physics, Particle Physics, Quantum Field Theory, Statistical Mechanics
majorContributions: In collaboration with Tsung-Dao Lee, Yang demonstrated that parity symmetry is not conserved in weak nuclear interactions, a revolutionary insight confirmed experimentally by Chien-Shiung Wu. For this achievement Yang and Lee received the 1957 Nobel Prize in Physics. In 1954, Yang and Robert Mills developed Yang-Mills theory, introducing non-Abelian gauge fields, a framework that became central to modern particle physics and the Standard Model. He also made major contributions to statistical mechanics, condensed matter physics, integrable systems, and quantum theory.
laterLife: Yang held prestigious appointments at the Institute for Advanced Study, Stony Brook University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Tsinghua University. Throughout his long career he remained one of the world's most respected physicists, mentoring researchers and contributing to the advancement of science internationally. His work earned numerous honors including the National Medal of Science, the Benjamin Franklin Medal, the Albert Einstein Medal, and the King Faisal Prize.
whyImportant: Chen Ning Yang helped establish the theoretical foundations of contemporary physics. The Yang-Mills framework underpins modern gauge theories describing the electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions. His Nobel Prize-winning work on parity violation overturned one of the most deeply held assumptions in physics and opened new directions in particle research. Many of today's advances in high-energy physics can be traced directly to his ideas and discoveries.
